units: <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 19:5">Lev. R. s. 19</cite> <he>רָפוּ ידיהן</he> their hands became lax (they lost their energy).—Part. pass. <cite ref="T00934"><he>רָפוּי</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="T00933"><he>רְפוּיָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 141b:9">Sabb. 141ᵇ</cite> <he>בר׳</he> when the shoe on the block is loose (can be taken off without moving the block).

<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 8:5">Mikv. VIII, 5</cite> <he>יְרַפֶּה כדי וכ׳</he> he must loosen his hold of the objects, so that the water can come in contact with them; Y. Ḥag. III, beg. 78ᵈ <he>יְרַפֵּם עד וכ׳</he> he must let them go until &c.

senses.gloss: to let hang down; to make lax, weaken. Tanḥ. K’dosh. 6 מְרַפִּין כנפיהם they let their wings hang down. Lev. R. l. c. (ref. to Is. XXXV, 3) שרִפִּיתֶם עצמיכם וכ׳ you weakened yourselves through your evil doings.
units: <cite ref="Bekhorot 5b">Bekh. 5ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 106a">Snh. 106ᵃ</cite> (play on <he>ר̇פ̇י̇ד̇י̇ם̇</he>) <he>שרִֹיפּ֗וּ י̇ד̇יהן מדברי תורה</he> (not <he>עצמן</he>) they let their hands drop from (holding) the words of the Law; Tanḥ.
<cite ref="Exodus 25">B’shall. 25</cite> <he>שרִפּוּ ידיהן מן התורה</he> (or <he>שרָפוּ</he>, v. supra); a. e.—Part. pass. <he>מְרוּפּה</he>; f. <cite ref="M02569"><he>מְרוּפָּה</he></cite>.
Sabb. 130ᵃ עדיין היא מר׳ בידם (not הוא; Ms. O. רְפוּיָה) it is still lax in their hands (they treat the ceremony with laxity), opp. מוחזקת held fast.—3) to soften, teach good manners.

<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 4:6">Ruth R. to II, 5</cite> <he>רבתה רִפְּתָה לה</he> (or <he>רָפְתָה</he>) her mistress (Naomi) had taught her good manners; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 601:20">Yalk. ib. 601</cite> <he>חמותה מאלפא לה</he>.
